messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: continuous-batcher service high memory growth on gpu-pool-usw-3, multiple CUDA OOMs observed; 3 containers crashed in last 4m. Root: continuous-batcher queue length > 5000 across shards. Alert id: CB-1970456789
Alice K: I’m on it. Pulling logs from the affected pods now.
Raj P: heads up — customer-facing routes might be impacted, I'm paging support to monitor error rate.
Maria L: Noted. Increasing throttle on ingress isn't automatic? We should do a soft-throttle asap.
Alice K: Logs show repeated allocation failures followed by "CUDA out of memory" and then runtime panics. Snippet:
```
2026-03-14T21:12:10Z batcher.c:542 allocate_kv_cache failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (error 2)
2026-03-14T21:12:10Z continuous_batcher.c:238 queue_length=5238 pending=1300 max_batch=1024
stack: runtime/panic at kv_cache.c:76
container: exit code 137
```
Alice K: There was a config change in last deploy that removed the enforced `max_inflight_batches` limit (PR #3421). Could be the root cause.
Chip (eng-runtime): That PR also changed how we compute dynamic batch window; if traffic pattern spikes it may let the batch grow unchecked. We're seeing batch growth -> KV cache blowup -> OOM cascade -> node flaps.
SRE Bot: auto-scaling event detected: node-replacement triggered after 2 container failures on gpu-pool-usw-3.
Raj P: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable queue backpressure toggle (runtime flag `--queue-throttle=on`) across the pool, 2) roll restart batcher workers with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher -n inference --grace-period=30`, 3) temporarily reduce shard concurrency via `shard.max_batch=128`. Who can execute steps 1-2?
Alice K: I can patch the helm override for `queueThrottle: true` and start rolling restarts. Doing that now — will stagger by 30s.
Maria L: I'll cut a traffic rule to route new requests to region-eu while we stabilize, to reduce pressure on USW. Creating a temporary route in the router service.
Chip (eng-runtime): Also enable `kv_cache.size_limit=8GB` as a safety cap until we revert PR #3421. I'll push a hotfix image with the safety checks.
Alice K: Patch applied, rollout started. Rolling restarts started: batcher-0 -> batcher-1 -> batcher-2 (staggered).
SRE Bot: Deploy monitoring: mem usage dropped on batcher-0 after restart, but batcher-2 still shows queue > 2000.
Raj P: Support reporting: customers seeing 30-60s latency spikes and a ~2% increase in 5xx on generation endpoints for the last 7 minutes. Key customers: acme-inc, finlytics. Notifying CSM.
Alice K: After forcing `--queue-throttle=on` on remaining pods, queue drain rate improved. Restarted the remaining 3 pods. Observed fewer OOMs.
Chip (eng-runtime): Hotfix image (r-inference:2026-03-14-hotfix-queuecap) rolled to 50% of pool. Contains guard rails to prevent batch_accumulate > 2048 and enforces KV cap.
Maria L: Router rule applied, ~22% of traffic rerouted to eu-region for 15m. Latency there is fine, so customers should see partial relief.
Raj P: Estimating customer impact window: ~21:12-21:28 UTC. Logged incidents for the customers affected.
Alice K: Observed one node (gpu-node-7) had kernel driver OOM logs; it was cordoned and drained as precaution. Node is in maintenance.
SRE Bot: Node replacement completed, new node joined cluster at 21:25:11 UTC.
Chip (eng-runtime): Recommended follow-ups: revert PR #3421 temporarily, add unit test for max_inflight enforcement, add e2e test to simulate traffic spike with KV cache caps, and add an alert for sustained queue_size > 1000 for >2m.
Raj P: I'll own customer comms summary and coordinate with CSM for post-incident notes.
Alice K: Handoff to next on-call (Maria) in 10m. Current state: queue sizes stabilizing (<300 across pods), no new OOMs in the last 6m, hotfix at 50% ramped.
Maria L: Acknowledged. I'll continue ramp and monitor 15m. Action items I'll take: finish 100% rollout of hotfix, revert PR on staging and prepare revert PR for prod, keep EU routing for 10m, and prepare postmortem draft.
Chip (eng-runtime): I'll open an internal ticket for kernel-driver logs on gpu-node-7 and coordinate with infra to run diagnostics.
Alice K: Thanks all. If anyone sees queue growth again ping me and @Chip.
Maria L: Oncall notes: handover -> monitoring urls: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/continuous-batcher, logs: kubectl logs -l app=continuous-batcher -n inference --tail=200, runbook section 'batcher emergency throttle'.
SRE Bot: Incident resolved state changed to: mitigated.
Raj P: Adding post-incident customer impact summary to the ticket. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.
Alice K: Quick root-cause hypothesis: PR #3421 removed a safety check that bounded in-flight batch accumulation; under a traffic spike that allowed continuous growth of batch accumulation leading to KV cache exhaustion and subsequent CUDA OOMs -> container crashes -> node replacement.
Maria L: Will add regression test and add a canary for queue-throttle default=true for future deploys.
Chip (eng-runtime): +1 on canary. Also recommend adding an automatic fallback to a smaller model variant when batcher queue > threshold to preserve tail latency for customer traffic.
Alice K: End of thread — handoff complete.
